concerns.title: Jimmy White — Machin & Associates, Elliot #1, alarm call closed 12:06 PM, job 35034. Gas sensor failure with a reading above zero. The form records the monitor triggering
concerns.text: "Upon arrival, monitor was triggered on sensor 4. Sensor 4 was hung at 27ppm and wouldn't drop off. Bad sensor element. Swapped sensor head and everything is working properly." The photo note adds: "Already taken off of stand and unplugged battery to kill power to board." Note that "Is any of our equipment damaged?" was answered "NO" on the same form while the manager-notification field carries "Jimmy White" and the explanation describes a failed sensor element — the answer and the narrative do not agree. Follow-up: confirm the failed sensor head is tagged out and off the fleet, and correct the damaged-equipment answer so the record matches the repair.

confirm.text: On the air job OWL forms, "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority utilized" sit in the same ten-item multi-select as routine positive selections. Kelby confirmed on 09/23 that flagging these is correct and that it is a training issue: technicians should only select stop-work authority when it was actually used, and may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard any wellhead work as inherently unsafe. These are listed as items needing the technician's confirmation, not as confirmed events.

"Unsafe conditions" selected alongside eight or nine positive items, with a complete and positive narrative — the mis-selection pattern. None of these forms contains any narrative describing an actual unsafe condition:
Nathan Contreras — Skaggs 8 2HB, 2:43 PM, job 35010_1. Narrative: "We observed a well realigned on a maintenance job."
Nathan Contreras — Charles Midkiff 38-47 4713 4703BH, 3:54 PM, job 35021_1. Narrative closes with "Nothing , job was perfect".
Nathan Contreras — University 10-1 10D, 10:06 AM, job 35027_1. Narrative: "We observed a disconnect done on a wellhead injection line."
Jose Campos — Lenorah Epley #7, 2:59 PM, job 34945_2. Narrative describes a normal vacuum operation with valves and gaskets changed out.
Michael Jobe — Scharbauer Ranch 2141H, 2:24 PM, job 35017_1. Narrative: "Had meeting went great went over everything that needed to be done."
Michael Jobe — Poppy Atrelle 21D 4H, 9:37 AM, job 35016_1. Narrative: "Had a good meeting went great went over what needed to be done in crew did good on safety."
Nathan Contreras and Jose Campos both appeared on this list on 09/23 as well. Contreras is on it three times today. That is worth one conversation rather than six.

Ruben Rojo — University 1-28 1H, 3:13 PM, job 34847_1. This one is different. "Unsafe conditions" is selected, and the entire Learn section of the close-out is blank — "One thing we'll do better next time", "Did we leave the location better than we found it?", "How did we leave this location better than we found it?" and "Location Name" all carry no entry. There is no positive narrative to offset the selection. Rojo was on this list on 09/23 as well, also with a blank close-out. Ask him directly what he selected it for.

Christian Lee 1099 — Owens Cravens W31D 4H, job 34967_2, form dated 09/23 and delivered 09/24. This one is different. He selected "Stop work authority utilized" — the stronger option, not "discussed". Both narrative continuation fields are empty and the Learn section is blank; the only content is "Did we leave the location better than we found it?: Yes". A stop-work-utilized selection with no narrative at all needs an answer.

Christian Lee 1099 — Pratt Vaughn 15N 114H, 9:09 AM, job 35018_2. Also selected "Stop work authority utilized", with only four items selected overall. The narrative reads "A very successful and quick reconnect" and the Learn entry is "Bring more water" — nothing describing a stop. Second stop-work-utilized selection from the same technician in two days.

Alejandro Najar — Dawkins Jones 40F 310H, 12:36 PM, job 35012_2. This one describes a real event. He selected "Stop work authority was discussed" rather than "utilized", but the narrative names what happened:
"stopped the job when the need of an angle grinder was talked about to cut off some rusted bolts that wouldnt break loose"

Alexander Clubb's form on the same job corroborates it: "Job scope was completed with only 1 minor issue, bolt on the flowline would come off so they had to cut it off... as crew was cutting the atmosphere was monitored." This reads as a genuine stop and hot-work control, correctly handled but recorded under the wrong selection.

A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review — I read the text the forms carry, not the images. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images and never as text, so nothing in this report should be taken as confirming those are current.
